content:
fast_instance% whnf-reduces terms, expecting a constructor application, and if any of the constructor arguments are typeclass arguments (square brackets binders) then it recurses into that argument's value.

I'm trying to surround the DecidableEq field of LinearOrder with square brackets so that it would infer when possible, and I've run into two issues with fast instances:

  1. To deal with families of instances (e.g. Π i, Group (G i)) fast_instance% telescopes down any foralls in the type. After #36420 this only happens for the top-level term and not the recursive ones. I think this is an unintended regression?

  2. It's pretty useful for LinearOrders to be fast_instance%s, but their DecidableEq field might fail to be for various reasons. Could we introduce some sort of fast_instance% (ignore := DecidableEq) ... to prevent recursing, or fast_instance% +loose ... to ignore failures?
I agree with both points. We could indeed have a fast_instance% +loose version.
+1 for mathlib playing fast and loose

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

I agree with both points.

Thanks! #43203 fixes the telescopes (I think). Apparently the top-level one also doesn't work:

import Mathlib.Tactic.FastInstance
def Foo := Unit
/--
error: Provided instance does not reduce to a constructor application
  fun a b => isTrue ⋯
-/
#guard_msgs (substring := true) in
example : DecidableEq Foo := fast_instance% fun a b ↦ isTrue rfl
